terms.definition: Coplanar lines that never intersect.
Lines that intersect to form right angles.
A line that intersects two or more coplanar lines at distinct points.
Angles in matching relative positions where a transversal crosses two lines.
Interior angles on opposite sides of a transversal.
Exterior angles on opposite sides of a transversal.
Interior angles on the same side of a transversal.
A statement formed by reversing the hypothesis and conclusion of a conditional statement.
The ratio of vertical change to horizontal change between two points on a nonvertical line.
The signed vertical change used when calculating slope.
The signed horizontal change used when calculating slope.
The slope of a vertical line, for which horizontal change is zero.
The slope of a horizontal line.
A number obtained by reversing a nonzero fraction and changing its sign; slopes of nonvertical perpendicular lines are negative reciprocals.
A coordinate formula derived from the Pythagorean theorem for finding the distance between two points.
The point that divides a segment into two congruent segments.
A proof that places figures in a coordinate plane and uses algebraic calculations to establish geometric properties.
An equation whose graph is a straight line.
The linear form y=mx+b, where m is slope and b is the y-intercept.
The linear form y-y1=m(x-x1), describing a line through a known point with a known slope.
The point or y-coordinate where a graph crosses the y-axis.
Lying on the same straight line.
